publication.title: Design of a 65-kW Wireless Charging Station Characterized by Optimal Load Impedance Tracking Control
publication.journal: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology

application.description: Static EV wireless charging prototype; author describes compatibility with SAE J2954.

prototype.coupler_type: Double-D coil couplers with ferrite and magnetic/electric shielding
prototype.gap_definition: Vertical ground-assembly to vehicle-assembly coupling-element separation
prototype.misalignment_description: Back-to-back tests report misalignment up to 60% of coil dimensions; positioning study gives Delta X approximately +/-0.21 m and Delta Y approximately +/-0.14 m under a stated efficiency-above-91% envelope.
prototype.control_method: Active optimal load-impedance tracking with primary and secondary control; switching frequency tracks resonant frequency.
prototype.institution: University of West Bohemia (with University of Zilina co-authorship)

input_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC1 at primary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration
excludes: Full 3-phase mains front end and complete battery/grid-recuperation chain

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC2 at the secondary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration

efficiency.definition: Back-to-back system efficiency plotted between author-labelled P_DC1 and P_DC2; not full WCS mains-to-battery efficiency.

measurements.load_description: Back-to-back test using an externally excited DC generator as source; output/load condition per figure 18.
measurements.alignment_description: Authors state back-to-back tests include misalignment evaluation up to 60% of coil dimensions.
measurements.source_locator: Primary article, section V.B, pp.4-5, text immediately preceding/after Fig.18.
measurements.notes: Highest reported efficiency among the operational states described in this back-to-back test section; input voltage limit constrained power to approximately 58 kW.

excludes: Full 3-phase mains front end and complete battery/grid-recuperation chain

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC2 at the secondary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration

efficiency.definition: Back-to-back system efficiency plotted between author-labelled P_DC1 and P_DC2; not full WCS mains-to-battery efficiency.

measurements.notes: Reported as >70 kW at 96.3%; the paper's nominal design rating is 65 kW. Keep actual test result distinct from nominal rating.

output_boundary.measurement_point: WCS output-side DC/DC boundary in the full chain; battery was represented by a grid-recuperation arrangement in the associated tests

efficiency.definition: η_WCS, authors' whole wireless charging system efficiency in Table VII at 65 kW for the proposed third control strategy.

measurements.load_description: Full-power 65 kW control-strategy comparison; authors distinguish whole-chain η_WCS from η_DC-DC.

measurements.notes: Do not substitute the 95.5% η_DC-DC subchain figure for the 92.7% η_WCS whole-chain figure. Table VII gives both metrics at 65 kW.

excludes: Battery and AC mains front end

lineage: One prototype / one publication with multiple distinct test modes and measurement boundaries; five measurements must not be counted as five independent prototype realizations.
limitations: Areas for transmitter and receiver couplers were not transcribed here because the cited sources' tabulated values were not identified in the accessible locator; missing values remain null.
Back-to-back test boundaries use author-labelled P_DC1/P_DC2 and are not the complete WCS/battery energy chain.
Authors state the grid-recuperation substitute in battery-load tests does not permit full-power testing.
Reported figures lack uncertainty intervals in the accessible text; no uncertainty is invented.
The 2026 survey is secondary for the 70 kW/96.3% summary; the 2025 paper is the primary source for the underlying operating point.
